big: Two investors each make ₹1 lakh. One sold equity fund units. The other sold a debt fund. Their tax bills can be very different, since each type of asset follows its own rules.

lines: Is the tax the same for shares, equity funds and debt funds?
No. Each follows its own rules, and Budgets change them. Learn the idea first, then always check the current rule.

intro: Plain pictures of the main cases.
rows: Short and long holding are taxed at different rates
For many, the gain is added to income and taxed at slab rate
Added to income and taxed at slab rate
A small tax added on each listed trade
note: Exact rates and limits change with each Budget. Check the current rule on the official tax site or with a tax adviser.

h: Made-up rates, to show the idea
alt: Two sets of bars comparing tax at assumed rates for an equity fund and a debt fund
caps: Two people, each with a ₹1 lakh gain.
The equity fund follows its own gains rate. Assume 10%.
The debt fund gain is added to income. Assume a 30% slab.
Assumed rates for the sums only. Real rates change, so check before acting.

q: Rohan sells units of a debt fund and makes a gain. How is it often taxed?
opts: At zero, since debt funds are safe
At a flat rate set by the fund house
Only after ten years of holding
why: Safety of a fund has no link to whether its gains are taxed.
For many debt funds, the gain is taxed at the investor's slab rate.
Tax rates are set by law and not by a fund house.
There is no rule that waits ten years before taxing a debt fund gain.

q: Meena gets a dividend from a fund. How does tax treat it?
opts: It is never taxed at any stage
It is taxed only if she reinvests
It is taxed at the fund's rate, never hers
It is taxed at her slab rate
why: Dividends are taxed, so they are not a tax-exempt income.
Tax falls on receiving the dividend, whether or not she reinvests.
The investor's own slab applies, and the fund's rate is not used.
Dividends are added to the investor's income and taxed at her slab rate.

opts: A bonus paid by the exchange to investors
A fee the bank charges for each new account
A small tax charged on listed trades
The tax on a salary credited every month
why: It is a charge, not a bonus, and it is paid by the investor.
Bank account fees are a separate matter from STT.
Securities transaction tax is added to certain trades on the exchange.
Salary tax is deducted from pay and has nothing to do with STT.

q: Rohan hears a friend say 'tax on funds is a flat 10% for everyone'. What should he do?
opts: Check the current rule for his type of fund
Accept it, as friends know the law
Assume the rate stays the same every year
Skip tax forms since it is flat
why: Rates differ by fund type and change, so check the current rule.
A friend's claim is not a source. Official rules are.
Rates are changed from time to time, so they are not fixed forever.
Tax forms are still needed, whatever the rate turns out to be.

pts: Equity and debt gains follow different rules.
Dividends are added to income and taxed at your slab rate.
Rates change with Budgets. Check the current rule before acting.
